bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program Record of Decision".
bill.latestActionText: Indefinitely postponed by Senate by Unanimous Consent.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), issued on December 9, 2024, and related to the record of decision (ROD) for the program that leases, develops, produces, and transports oil and gas in and from the Coastal Plain program area within the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. The 2024 ROD that is being nullified by this resolution replaced the 2020 ROD that made all of the approximately 1.6 million acres of the program area available for oil and gas leasing. The 2024 ROD adopted Alternative D2 in the 2024 Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program Final Supplemental Environmental Impact Statement, which made approximately 1.2 million acres unavailable for leasing or exploration in order to protect and conserve resources and certain uses in these areas. However, the 2024 ROD requires the statutory minimum of 400,000 acres to be made available for oil and gas leasing in a specified lease sale, subject to certain stipulations and operating procedures. Under current law, those acres must be located in the areas with the highest potential for the discovery of hydrocarbons.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution would overturn a December 2024 Bureau of Land Management decision that restricted oil and gas leasing in Alaska's Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. The 2024 rule made about 1.2 million acres unavailable for leasing while keeping the legally required minimum of 400,000 acres open. If this resolution passes, it would nullify that restriction and potentially allow the earlier 2020 decision—which opened all 1.6 million acres to leasing—to govern instead.

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects oil and gas leasing rights and acreage availability in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Coastal Plain.
Environmental and conservation organizations have direct stakes in decisions governing wildlife refuge land use and protection.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the rule submitted by the federal land agency, issued on December 9, 2024, and related to the record of decision for the program that leases, develops, produces, and transports oil and gas in and from the Coastal Plain program area within the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys fuel or heats a home. People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what fuel costs. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
